note.headline: Small caps and health care lead while rates back up and mega-cap tech lags
note.standfirst: The Russell 2000 rose +1.65% and health care gained +2.37% while the Nasdaq 100 slipped -0.13%, a rotation out of the winners' trade and into cyclicals and defensives. Positioning into month-end should note the curve is bear steepening even as equity vol compresses, a combination that rewards breadth over concentration.
takeaways: Small caps and cyclical sectors outperformed while mega-cap tech lagged, with the Russell 2000 up +1.65% against the Nasdaq 100 down -0.13%.
The Treasury curve bear steepened, with 10-year yields up 6bp to 5.15% and 2s10s widening 3bp to 38bp.
Volatility fell hard across the surface, with VIX down -6.13% to 17.31 and VVIX down -9.15%, even as the MOVE index ticked up.
High yield credit sits at session lows alongside leveraged loans, a soft spot inside an otherwise constructive risk tape.
note.desk_view:
The session confirms a rotation theme more than a risk-off or risk-on one. Breadth was positive at 1.27 advancers to decliners and dispersion ran at 1.28, consistent with money moving between sectors rather than leaving equities. Health care led on LLY, UNH and PFE, all up more than 2%, while communications and tech names, NFLX, META, GOOGL and AAPL, gave back ground. The S&P 500 closed up +0.28%, a muted headline number that hides the rotation underneath.

The level that decides whether this is healthy or a warning sign is the 10-year yield at 5.15%, now up 6bp on the day and at the top end of its recent range. Bear steepening with equities still bid is a tolerable combination, but it depends on the long end not pushing through resistance. The 30-year sits at 5.48%, up 5bp. If the back end extends through these levels while VIX keeps falling, the rates and equity vol signals will be telling two different stories, and one of them is wrong.
watching: 30-year Treasury auction demand and whether foreign bid holds at these yield levels.
Whether health care leadership extends beyond LLY, UNH and PFE earnings reactions.
High yield spreads, with HYG and JNK sitting at lows, for signs of credit stress spreading to equities.
Dollar index follow-through below 101.71 after today's -0.26% move.
note.equities:
The headline indices told a split story. The Dow rose +1.02% and the Russell 2000 gained +1.65%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell -0.13%. The S&P 500 added +0.28%, landing in between, consistent with a market trading sector rotation rather than a directional call on risk.

Health care was the standout sector at +2.37%, with LLY, UNH and PFE all posting gains above 2%. Financials rose +1.20% and real estate added +1.70%, both benefiting from the small-cap bid. Technology was the weak sector at -0.28%, dragged by AAPL, GOOGL and META. Breadth confirmed the rotation story: 14 advancers against 11 decliners, a ratio of 1.27, with dispersion at 1.28 pointing to real divergence under the index level rather than a uniform move.
note.rates:
The curve bear steepened across the session. Yields rose at every tenor from the 1-month out to 30-year, with the belly and long end moving more than the front: 2-year up 3bp to 4.77%, 10-year up 6bp to 5.15%, 30-year up 5bp to 5.48%. 2s10s widened 3bp to 38bp and 3m10y widened 5bp to 88bp, while 5s30s held flat at 54bp.

The MOVE index ticked up 0.39% to 101.70, a small gain against a backdrop of falling equity vol, a divergence worth flagging. Real yields did the heavy lifting: the 10-year TIPS yield rose 6bp to 2.80%, while the 10-year breakeven was unchanged at 2.35% and the 5y5y forward breakeven slipped 1bp to 2.32%. The move higher in yields looks driven by real rates, not inflation expectations.
note.credit: Credit sent a mixed signal against the equity tape. Investment grade (LQD) rose 0.33% and EM sovereign debt (EMB) added 0.14%, both constructive, but US high yield closed flat on HYG and fell -0.02% on JNK, with both sitting at session lows alongside leveraged loans, which fell -0.10%. The divergence between IG strength and HY weakness is the detail to carry into tomorrow: it is not yet spreading, but it is not improving either.
note.fx: The dollar index fell -0.26% to 101.71, its weakness broad-based against G10. EUR/USD rose 0.13% to 1.124, GBP/USD gained 0.34% to 1.338, and AUD/USD rose 0.48% to 0.701. USD/CHF fell -0.29% while USD/JPY bucked the dollar-soft trend, rising 0.22% to 158.16. In EM, USD/BRL fell -0.72% and USD/MXN fell -0.18%, both dollar-negative, while USD/TRY rose 0.08% to a fresh high of 49.56, extending its own trend independent of the broad dollar move.
note.commodities: Energy fell hard: WTI dropped -5.22% to $98.25 and natural gas fell -2.13%, while Brent held up better at -0.36%. Precious metals were mixed, gold down -0.44% to $4,142 even as silver rose 1.92% and platinum gained 1.29%. Copper continued its run, up 1.17% to $6.615 and sitting near highs for the year. Grains and softs were broadly weaker, wheat down -1.91% and coffee down -1.77%.
note.volatility: The vol surface compressed hard. VIX fell -6.13% to 17.31, VIX9D fell -9.26% to 16.27, and VVIX dropped -9.15% to 97.15, all pointing to cheaper near-dated protection. SKEW fell -3.99% to 161.86, suggesting tail hedging demand eased alongside the broad decline in implied vol. The one outlier is the MOVE index, up slightly to 101.70, a reminder that rate vol is not following equity vol lower.
note.digital: Digital assets traded with a modest positive beta to the risk rally. Bitcoin rose 1.10% to $82,752.61, Ether gained 1.72%, and XRP led majors with a 2.37% gain. The moves were consistent with the broader rotation into cyclical risk rather than a standalone crypto story.
note.international: European markets closed softer ahead of the US session, with the EURO STOXX 50 down -0.38% and the CAC 40 down -0.38%, while the SMI bucked the trend at +0.76%. Asia was mixed: the KOSPI rose 1.76% and the Hang Seng gained 0.52%, while the Nikkei fell -0.62% and the Sensex dropped -1.17%. The handoff to New York was neutral to soft, with the US session's small-cap and health care bid developing independent of the overseas tape.
note.correlation:
The standout cross-asset signal is equity vol and rate vol pulling apart. VIX fell -6.13% while the MOVE index rose slightly, a split that typically does not last. Equities read the session as calm, bonds read it as unsettled, and the gap between the two usually closes through one market catching down or up to the other.

A break in that correlation matters because the current equity rally into small caps and cyclicals assumes financing conditions stay orderly. If the 10-year keeps rising and the MOVE index follows through with a genuine move rather than a one-day tick, the small-cap and real estate leadership seen today becomes harder to sustain, since both sectors carry the most interest rate sensitivity in the index.
